subject: Proposal: mid-term Dedicated uplift & GPU pool amendment
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@neptunelabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: mid-term Dedicated uplift & GPU pool amendment

Hi Lena —

Quick note following Neptune's spike in usage last month. Your Dedicated pool is routinely hitting sustained utilization beyond the committed baseline (we see prolonged 90%+ GPU utilization windows during overnight ET batches). To avoid throttling and to keep unit cost predictable, I put together a short amendment proposal to: 1) add 8 GPUs to the existing Dedicated pool (A100-equivalent), 2) increase the reserved commit from 64 to 120 GPU-hours/day equivalent, and 3) provide a 12-month price amendment with a mid-term uplift proration so you don’t pay full-term twice.

High level:
- New pool sizing: +8 GPUs (target: handle additional 1.8x peak throughput)
- Committed throughput guarantee: sustained 1.2M tokens/min across the pool (95th pct latency targets included)
- Pricing: I’ve sketched a mid-term uplift discount (see attached pdf) — 18% off list for a 12-month extension with monthly billing. If we agree to a 24-month commit we can improve to ~23%.

I'm including a draft quote and a throughput projection spreadsheet. Can you confirm procurement timing? If you want, we can lock a provisional short-term burst buffer while the amendment completes to avoid any throttling risk.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call today or tomorrow.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: Neptune_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf (draft quote), throughput_projection_neptune.xlsx (projection), amendment_pricing_table.csv (pricing breakdown)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: mid-term Dedicated uplift & GPU pool amendment

Diego —

Thanks for the send. Couple of asks before we present a final number to Neptune:
1) Margin floor — finance wants to see us hold at least 18% gross margin on this amendment unless Marissa/RevenueOps okays a lower threshold.
2) Can Karthik validate the throughput/latency assumptions in the spreadsheet? We need explicit SLO language to include in the amendment.
3) Any references to proration and billing alignment with their existing commit? Put the proration logic inline in the PDF to avoid procurement questions.

If we need more room on discount, please note the up-sell probability and ARR delta in your ask to leadership.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Park <lena.park@neptunelabs.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@neptunelabs.ai>, ops@neptunelabs.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: mid-term Dedicated uplift & GPU pool amendment

Diego —

Appreciate the quick response and the draft. A few items from our side:
- Confirm total monthly committed spend after the uplift (we need the exact number for our budget owners).
- We need a throughput SLA (95th pct P99 latency target and a definition of what constitutes a breach). Please include remediation (credits or auto-failover to burst) and an escalation contact.
- Procurement asked whether the 18% is the best you can do for a 12-month term; they flagged that our internal budgeting committee prefers net-30 terms (we currently have net-45).
- We also want to understand proration: will the uplift be pro-rated to the next billing cycle or bill instantly (they prefer aligned billing).

Can you get back with a single PDF that has price lines, proration example, and SLA bullets? If acceptable, procurement is ready to review within 72 hours.

Regards,
Lena
VP, Platform & Ops
Neptune Labs
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@neptunelabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: mid-term Dedicated uplift & GPU pool amendment

Lena —

Thanks — stacked answers below and attached an updated quote (Neptune_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf) that includes a proration example. Key points:

1) Monthly committed spend after uplift (example pricing line)
- Current baseline (committed): $48,000/month (64 GPU-hours/day baseline equivalent)
- Post-uplift committed: $83,200/month (120 GPU-hours/day equivalent, +8 GPUs added to pool)
- Price shown is net after the 18% amendment discount for a 12-month extension. 24-month option with 23% net is shown as an alternate line in the PDF.

2) SLA and remediation
- SLO: 95th percentile latency target for interactive calls is 220ms (per-sequence, standard prompt). For bulk batch jobs we include a throughput floor: sustained 1.2M tokens/min across the pool for the committed window.
- Remedy: If we miss the agreed SLA for two consecutive billing cycles, Neptune may elect either a 10% bill credit for the affected period or an automatic temporary burst to Hosted tier at no charge until we restore capacity.
- Primary escalation: infra-ops@redwood.ai (24x7) and your AE escalation (cc'd). We can add a named engineer for your account in the contract if you prefer.

3) Proration & billing alignment
- Uplift will be pro-rated to the start of the next billing cycle by default. We included a worked example in the attached PDF showing proration if the amendment executes mid-cycle. If you need immediate capacity before billing alignment, we can enable a short-term burst buffer for up to 14 days with separate usage line items (we typically avoid double-billing).

4) Payment terms
- Standard Redwood terms: net-45. For Neptune we can approve net-30 for the 12-month amendment contingent on an executed amendment and an initial month payment within 30 days of signature (finance has approved net-30 for this deal).

I've asked Karthik to validate the throughput assumptions and attached his projection sheet. If this aligns with procurement, we can route the amendment to DocuSign and lock the provisional burst buffer while the DocuSign completes.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Neptune_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf, throughput_projection_neptune.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: mid-term Dedicated uplift & GPU pool amendment — throughput validation

Diego/Team —

Quick validation notes after modeling Neptune's recent job cadence (see throughput_projection_neptune.xlsx):
- Adding +8 A100-equivalent GPUs gives ~1.9x headroom at current job mix (small beam search + batch scoring).
- With prefix KV caching for repeated prompts we estimate effective token throughput improvement of ~20% which lowers peak contention risk.
- The sustained 1.2M tokens/min floor is achievable if Neptune agrees to the scheduled maintenance window (we need a 2-hour weekly window) and we enable auto-batching at the runtime layer.
- Risk: if Neptune shifts large synchronous RLHF-style jobs into the same pool without isolation, P99 latency could spike; recommend we include an isolation policy in the amendment (automatic routing to a separate burst chunk or dedicated queue).

I updated the spreadsheet with two conservative and optimistic scenarios and flagged the assumptions. Happy to be on the procurement call for the SLA language.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lena Park <lena.park@neptunelabs.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@neptunelabs.ai>, ops@neptunelabs.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: mid-term Dedicated uplift & GPU pool amendment

Diego/Marissa —

Thanks — procurement reviewed the updated PDF and the SLA bullets. We're comfortable moving forward on the 12-month amendment at the 18% net discount with the net-30 payment term, provided the DocuSign reflects the proration example and the two-hour weekly maintenance window.

Next steps: please route the amendment to DocuSign (cc procurement) and enable the provisional 14-day burst buffer starting Monday so our jobs don't throttle while legal signs off. We'll review the throughput spreadsheet with ops this afternoon and confirm any final isolation requests.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Lena
VP, Platform & Ops
Neptune Labs
